frameworks.name: SBP Enterprise Technology Governance & Risk Management Framework

controls.title: Security policies are approved, published and accepted
Information security risk is assessed and treated

User access is reviewed on a defined cycle

Privileged and root access is restricted and protected
Customer data is encrypted at rest
Data in transit uses TLS 1.2 or higher
Security logs are enabled and kept for 12 months
Backups are taken and restore-tested quarterly
Critical vulnerabilities are fixed within SLA
Code changes are peer-reviewed before merge
Endpoints are encrypted, locked and monitored
Networks are segmented and protected by a WAF
Physical access to facilities is controlled
Security awareness training is completed yearly
Background checks are completed before access
Assets are inventoried and owned
Security monitoring and alerting is in place
Suppliers are assessed by risk tier before and during use
Incident response plan is maintained and exercised
Business continuity and DR plans are tested yearly
Records of processing activities are maintained
Data subject rights requests are handled in time
Sanctions lists are refreshed within 24 hours
Transactions are monitored for suspicious activity
AI systems are inventoried, classified and impact-assessed
High-risk AI systems have human oversight
UAE IA Tier 2 baseline controls are implemented
Data is handled lawfully under PECA 2016
Board and management oversee security and technology risk
Security strategy and measurable objectives are set
Legal, regulatory and contractual requirements are identified and tracked
Security is built into project and change initiatives
Independent internal audit of security and technology controls
Management review and continual improvement of the management system
Context, interested parties and scope of the management system are defined
Documented information is controlled and versioned
Security performance is measured and reported
Contact with authorities and special interest groups is maintained
Nonconformities and corrective actions are managed
Competence and resources for security are provided
Risk management methodology, criteria and appetite are defined
Risk assessments are performed periodically and on significant change
Risk treatment plans and risk acceptance are approved by the right authority
Business impact analysis identifies critical functions and tolerances
Threat intelligence is collected, analysed and acted on
Systems are categorised and security authorised before operation
Continuous monitoring strategy for controls and risk
Inventory of information assets and systems with named owners
Information is classified and labelled
Acceptable use and return of assets
Media handling and secure disposal or reuse of equipment
Secure configuration baselines are defined and enforced
Software inventory and restrictions on installation
Access is granted through an approved joiner and mover process
Passwords and secrets are managed securely
Least privilege and need-to-know are enforced
Remote access is secured and monitored
Service and system accounts are governed
Access to source code and administrative tools is restricted
Access decisions are made per request by a policy engine and enforcement point
User and device posture are evaluated continuously for access
Resources are micro-segmented and communications secured regardless of location
Cryptographic keys are managed through their lifecycle
Data leakage is prevented and monitored
Data masking and protected test data
Data retention and secure deletion schedules are applied
Data location and cross-border transfers are controlled
Privacy notices and transparency to data subjects
Data subject rights requests are handled on time
Collection limitation and data minimisation
Privacy impact assessments for high-risk processing
Personal data sharing and processor agreements
Personal data breaches are notified within legal deadlines
Capacity and performance are managed
Malware protection is deployed and updated
System clocks are synchronised
Security events are monitored and alerted 24x7
Security events are analysed, correlated and triaged
Operating procedures are documented
Transaction and data integrity controls in processing
Network traffic is filtered and network services secured
Email and web filtering protect users
Wireless networks are secured
Communications are protected against denial of service
Penetration tests and resilience tests are performed
Security patches are applied on a defined schedule
Secure development lifecycle and security requirements
Security testing of applications before release
Development, test and production environments are separated
Outsourced development is supervised
Changes are assessed, approved, tested and recorded
Mobile devices and BYOD are managed
Terms of employment and confidentiality agreements include security duties
Disciplinary process for security breaches
Responsibilities after termination or change of role
Remote working is secured
Equipment, cabling and utilities are protected
Clear desk and clear screen
Secure areas and data centres are monitored
Supplier agreements include security, audit and exit clauses
Cloud services are acquired, used and exited securely
Concentration risk and exit strategies for critical ICT providers
Register of ICT third-party arrangements is maintained
Incidents are detected, classified and escalated
Major incidents are reported to regulators within deadlines
Evidence is collected and preserved for investigation
Lessons learned from incidents are applied
ICT redundancy and recovery capability meet recovery objectives
Crisis communication plans for customers, staff and regulators
Lawful requests from authorities are verified, handled and logged
Traffic and subscriber data are retained as required by law
Intellectual property and licensing are respected
Records are protected against loss, falsification and unauthorised access
Unlawful online content and cybercrime complaints are handled
Critical data is stored and processed within the required jurisdiction
Regulatory security audits and certifications for critical systems
Equipment and suppliers for critical infrastructure are security-vetted
Coordination with the national CERT and sector regulator

AI risks are assessed and treated
Information about AI systems is provided to users and interested parties
AI suppliers and customer responsibilities are allocated
Human oversight and monitoring of AI system performance
Biometric presentation attack detection is evaluated and tested
Biometric data is protected and deleted after use
Biometric error and attack-detection rates are monitored
Concerns and whistleblowing can be raised safely
Statement of applicability is maintained
Privacy complaints and redress are handled
Privacy programme governance and accountability
Identity proofing before credentials are issued
Sessions lock, time out and limit failed logins
Insider threat programme
Environmental protection: fire, power, water and climate
Supply chain integrity, tamper and counterfeit protection
DNS, routing and domain security
Incident cost and impact are estimated and recorded
Accessibility of services for persons with disabilities
Online platform registration, complaints and content removal duties

findings.title: High: unpatched edge service exploitable
findings.rec: Patch to current release and add to patch SLA monitoring

issues.title: Agree 7-day patch SLA with service owners

risks.title: Ransomware via unpatched edge service
risks.desc: An internet-facing service misses a patch SLA and is exploited by ransomware, encrypting production data.

risks.title: Insider misuse of privileged access
risks.desc: A privileged user abuses standing access to exfiltrate or alter customer data.

risks.title: Sub-processor data breach of KYC data
risks.desc: A critical sub-processor holding KYC data suffers a breach, exposing customer identity records.

risks.title: Model bias in automated screening
risks.desc: The screening model produces biased outcomes, creating fair-treatment and regulatory exposure.

risks.title: Key person dependency on platform
risks.desc: Platform knowledge is concentrated in one engineer, risking continuity if they are unavailable.

risks.title: Phishing leading to credential theft
risks.desc: Staff are phished and credentials are stolen, bypassing perimeter controls.

risks.title: Non-compliance with EU AI Act
risks.desc: High-risk AI systems are not fully assessed against EU AI Act obligations before the deadline.

risks.title: Cloud misconfiguration exposes storage
risks.desc: A storage bucket is left public through misconfiguration, exposing data.

risks.title: Prolonged outage of core service
risks.desc: A core dependency fails for an extended period, breaching availability commitments.

risks.title: Cross-border data residency breach
risks.desc: KYC data is processed outside its required region, breaching PDPL and DIFC residency rules.

risks.title: Single-cloud concentration risk
risks.desc: Heavy reliance on one cloud provider concentrates availability and supply risk; accepted by management.

risks.title: Sanctions screening false-negative
risks.desc: A sanctioned party is not flagged by screening, creating regulatory and reputational exposure.

ai.name: KYC Screening Model v3
ai.basis: ISO 42001 and EU AI Act high-risk

tests.name: MFA enforced on all admin consoles
tests.logic: For every admin account, require factors >= 2 and status = enforced.

tests.name: TLS 1.2+ on public endpoints
tests.logic: Each public host negotiates TLS >= 1.2 and no weak ciphers.

tests.name: Disk encryption on managed laptops
tests.logic: Every managed endpoint reports full-disk encryption = on.

tests.name: Backup restore verified quarterly
tests.logic: A restore test is recorded within the last 90 days with RTO/RPO met.

tests.name: Logging and monitoring coverage
tests.logic: Critical services emit logs and have an active monitor.

tests.name: Vulnerability SLA adherence
tests.logic: No open critical finding older than the remediation SLA.
